mainTopic: Carrying between domains: passing through exempt air, narrow walls that create a רשות היחיד, and partitions created or removed at the moment of lifting or placing
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching about a pit (בור) in the public domain. To draw from it on שבת you need a ten-טפחים partition, and to drink you must put your head and most of your body inside. Next, רב מרדכי asks whether a person is חייב for throwing an object onto a column ten high and four wide, since on its way up the object passes through the exempt air above ten טפחים. The sages point to the משנה that rules one who places on top of such a structure is חייב. רב מרדכי deflects this: the משנה may be about a needle slid in through a protrusion or groove below ten. רבי יוחנן then asks about a wall less than four wide that turns an enclosed כרמלית into a רשות היחיד. עולא and a report in רבי יוחנן's own name rule by קל וחומר that throwing onto that wall makes one חייב. רבי יוחנן also asks what happens when lifting or placing an object happens at the same moment that a pit's ten-טפחים partition is created or removed. A proof from the fig cake (דבילה שמינה) is rejected. רבא's question about a board thrown with an object riding on it ends in תיקו. Finally רבא begins discussing what counts as placement on water, a topic that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rules for using a pit in the public domain on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The text finishes a teaching about a pit in a public domain. You may not draw water from it unless a ten-טפחים partition surrounds it. You may only drink if you put your head and most of your body inside. The pit's depth and its raised bank combine to make ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Unless they built a partition around it ten handbreadths high. And one may not drink from it on שבת unless he puts his head and most of his body into it. And a pit and its raised bank combine to make up ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that started on the previous amud. It explains how a person can take water from a pit that sits in a public area on שבת without carrying between domains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pit counts as a private domain, and the area around it is public. Drawing water out moves it from private to public, so a ten-טפחים partition is needed to make the surrounding area private too. When drinking, putting your head and most of your body into the pit means you are drinking 'inside' the private domain, so nothing is carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: partition or wall that creates a separate domain
his head and most of his body
its raised bank or rim (around the pit)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the basic idea behind the whole discussion: ten טפחים of height or depth is what turns a spot into its own private domain.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִיצָה
phrases.english: unless they made a partition for it
phrases.notes: This finishes a rule from the previous amud: you may not draw water from the pit unless...

phrases.english: ten handbreadths high,
and one may not drink from it on Shabbat
unless he inserted into it
his head and most of his body.
And a pit and its bank join together to make ten.
phrases.notes: The pit's depth plus the height of its rim are added together to reach the ten טפחים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן עָשׂוּ לָהּ מְחִיצָה גְּבוֹהָה עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a teaching begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To draw from a pit in the public domain you need a ten-טפחים partition. To drink you must put your head and most of your body inside. The pit and its rim combine to reach ten.

steps.title: רב מרדכי asks about throwing onto a tall column
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי asks רבא about a column in the public domain that is ten טפחים high and four wide. If someone throws an object onto it, is he חייב? Or is he פטור because the object passed through exempt airspace on the way?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי asked רבא: A column in the public domain is ten handbreadths high and four wide. Someone threw an object, and it landed on top of the column. What is the law? Do we say the lifting was forbidden and the placing was forbidden, so he is liable? Or perhaps, since the object arrives from an exempt place, he is not liable?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins here. רב מרדכי wants to know whether throwing something onto a tall column in a public street makes a person חייב on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The column is a private domain because it is ten high and four wide. The object was picked up (עקירה) in the public domain and set down (הנחה) in the private one, which normally means חייב. The problem is the path in between. To land on top of the column, the object had to fly above ten טפחים, and that air is a מקום פטור. Maybe that 'break' in the middle cancels the liability.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked of him (introduces a question)
lifting an object from its place (the start of carrying)
setting an object down (the end of carrying)
an exempt area, which is neither public nor private

steps.confusionAlert: The object is not being moved from a מקום פטור. It starts in the public domain and ends in the private domain. The only question is whether passing through the exempt air above ten טפחים on the way breaks the act of carrying.

phrases.english: Rav Mordekhai asked of Rava:
a column in the public domain
ten high and four wide,
phrases.notes: These measurements make the top of the column a private domain.

phrases.english: and one threw and it landed on top of it — what is the law?
Do we say: the lifting was in a forbidden manner,
phrases.notes: The object was lifted from the public domain.

phrases.english: the placing was in a forbidden manner.
phrases.notes: The object was set down in the private domain.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּמִמְּקוֹם פְּטוּר קָאָתְיָא — לָא.
phrases.english: Or perhaps: since it comes from an exempt place — not.
phrases.notes: Just before landing, the object was in the air above ten טפחים, which is a מקום פטור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about domains and height, after the pit discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does passing through the exempt airspace above ten טפחים on the way cancel liability for throwing an object from the public domain onto a private-domain column?

steps.title: Three sages answer that the משנה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: רבא, רב יוסף and אביי each tell רב מרדכי that the answer is already in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: It is our משנה. He went and asked רב יוסף, who said to him: It is our משנה. He went and asked אביי, who said to him: It is our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי takes his question to three great sages one after another. All three give the same short answer: 'It's in our משנה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה they mean rules that one who places an object on top of a structure ten high and four wide in the public domain is חייב. They understand that ruling to cover our case, even though the object passes above ten טפחים on its way up.

keyTerms.meaning: it is (already taught in) our משנה

phrases.english: He said to him: It is our Mishnah.
He came and asked Rav Yosef,
he said to him: It is our Mishnah.
He came and asked Abaye,
he said to him: It is our Mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה already rules that one is חייב for placing an object on top of such a structure, so the thrower here is also חייב.

steps.title: רב מרדכי rejects the repeated answer
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי tells them they are all 'spitting the same spit.' Each one repeated the same answer, and he does not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You are all spitting each other's spit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי is not convinced. He complains that all three gave him the same answer, which he thinks does not really solve his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His sharp phrase means they are all copying one another without real thought. This is a rejection of their proof. It sets up the next step, where they will spell out exactly which משנה they mean.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: כּוּלְּכוּ בְּרוּקָּא דַהֲדָדֵי תָּפִיתוּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: All of you are spitting each other's spit.
phrases.notes: A colorful way of saying: you are all repeating the same weak answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה settles the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated yet. He only says the answer is unsatisfying. He explains why in step 6.

steps.title: The sages quote the משנה: placing on top makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The sages ask רב מרדכי whether he really disagrees. They quote the משנה: one who takes from such structures or places on top of them is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: And don't you agree? But we learned in the משנה: One who takes from them or places on top of them is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: Here the sages spell out their proof. They quote the exact words of the משנה that they believe answers the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person places an object on top of a structure ten high, the object normally rises above ten טפחים before it comes down. That means it passes through the exempt air. Yet the משנה still says חייב. So, they argue, passing through the מקום פטור does not cancel liability.

keyTerms.meaning: you hold or agree with this reasoning

phrases.english: They said to him: And you, do you not hold so?
But we learned: one who takes from them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means structures such as a rock or a wall that are ten high and four wide in the public domain.

phrases.english: and places on top of them — is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: הַנּוֹטֵל מֵהֶן וְנוֹתֵן עַל גַּבָּן — חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב מרדכי's rejection by quoting the source explicitly.
steps.raayaObject: That passing through the exempt air above ten טפחים does not cancel liability.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: one who takes from them or places on top of them is חייב.

steps.title: רב מרדכי: maybe the משנה is about a needle
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי answers that the משנה might be talking about a needle. A needle is so thin it can be placed without passing through the exempt air, so the משנה does not prove anything about his case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Perhaps our משנה is speaking about a needle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי pushes back against their proof. He suggests the משנה may be speaking about a special case that does not involve the exempt air at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A needle is tiny and takes up almost no space. It can be put on the column without ever entering the air above ten טפחים. If that is the case of the משנה, then the משנה never addressed an object passing through a מקום פטור, so his question remains open.
steps.whatToRemember: The sages say the משנה shows that passing through the exempt air above ten does not cancel liability. רב מרדכי replies that the משנה may only be about a needle, which never passes through that air. So his question about a thrown object stays open for now.

phrases.english: He said to them: Perhaps the Mishnah is about a needle.
phrases.notes: A needle can be set down without passing through the exempt area above ten טפחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה about placing on top of a structure.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may be talking about a needle, which never passes through the מקום פטור. So it does not cover a normal thrown object.

steps.title: Even a needle must rise a little
steps.stepSummary: The sages challenge רב מרדכי: even a needle has to be lifted slightly, so it too passes through the exempt air above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A needle, too, cannot be put there without being lifted a little!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages attack רב מרדכי's answer from Step 6. They say the needle case does not escape the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרדכי said a needle could be placed on the column without passing through exempt air. The sages argue that you cannot place anything, even a needle, without raising it at least a tiny bit. If so, the needle also passes above the column's top, and the משנה's ruling of חייב would answer his question after all.

phrases.english: A needle, too, it is impossible
phrases.notes: Responds directly to רב מרדכי's needle answer.

phrases.english: that it not be raised a little!
phrases.notes: Any lifting means it passes through the air above the top.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחַט נָמֵי אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא מִדַּלְיָא פּוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the needle answer given in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרדכי's claim that a needle can be placed without passing through exempt air.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing any object requires lifting it at least slightly. So even a needle passes through the air above the column, and the משנה should still settle the question.

steps.title: A protrusion or a groove below ten
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי gives two cases where the needle never rises above ten טפחים: the structure has a protrusion, or the needle goes into a groove.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the structure has a protrusion. Or, alternatively, the needle is placed into a groove.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי defends his needle answer. He describes two cases where the needle reaches the private domain without ever rising above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the structure has a small protrusion below ten טפחים. It counts like a hole in the private domain, so placing the needle there makes one חייב. In the second case, the needle is pushed sideways into a groove below ten, so it never enters the exempt air. Either way, the משנה can be explained without answering רב מרדכי's question, so his question stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the needle rises above the top and then comes down. In both cases the whole point is that it never rises above ten טפחים at all.
steps.whatToRemember: רב מרדכי's question is not settled by the משנה. The משנה can be read as a needle placed directly into the private domain without passing through exempt air.

phrases.english: That it has a protrusion.
phrases.notes: The protrusion is below ten and counts like a hole in the private domain.

phrases.english: Alternatively, that it is placed in a groove.
phrases.notes: The needle enters the groove sideways, below ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the needle case is defined so the needle never rises above ten.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any placement requires lifting, so the needle must cross the exempt air.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through a protrusion or a groove, the needle goes straight into the private domain below ten. So the משנה proves nothing about the thrown object.

steps.title: A narrow wall that encloses a private domain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks about a wall that is ten טפחים high but less than four wide, which turns an enclosed כרמלית into a רשות היחיד. If one throws an object onto the wall, is he חייב?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מיישא said that רבי יוחנן asked: There is a wall in the public domain that is ten טפחים high and less than four wide. It surrounds a כרמלית and turns it into a private domain. If someone throws an object and it lands on top of the wall, what is the law? Do we say that since the wall is not four wide, its top is a מקום פטור? Or perhaps, since the wall made the area a private domain, we view it as if the space were filled in?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי יוחנן asks whether the top of a narrow wall counts as part of the private domain it creates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a surface less than four טפחים wide is a מקום פטור, so landing there is not liable. But this wall is the very partition that makes the enclosed area a רשות היחיד. Perhaps it joins that area, as if the whole space were filled up to the top, and then it would count as private domain.

keyTerms.meaning: an in-between domain, neither fully public nor fully private
an exempt area (no liability for carrying to or from it)
it is considered as if it were filled in

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מְיָשָׁא, בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Meyasha said: Rabbi Yochanan asked:
A wall in the public domain
ten handbreadths high and not four wide
and it surrounds a karmelit
and made it into a private domain,
phrases.notes: The wall serves as the partition for the enclosed area.

phrases.english: and one threw and it landed on top of it, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דְּאֵינוֹ רָחָב אַרְבַּע —
phrases.english: Do we say: since it is not four wide —
phrases.notes: This is the side of the question that says he is exempt.

phrases.english: it is an exempt place,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דַּעֲשָׂאוֹ רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד —
phrases.english: or perhaps: since it made it a private domain —
phrases.notes: This is the side of the question that says he is liable.

phrases.english: it is considered as if it were filled in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about domains. The earlier column was four wide; this wall is narrower than four, so its top would normally be a מקום פטור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the top of a narrow wall a מקום פטור, or part of the רשות היחיד it creates?

steps.title: עולא's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers with a קל וחומר: the wall makes other space into a private domain, so it surely makes itself one.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is a קל וחומר. If the wall makes a partition for other areas, then surely it does so for itself!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רבי יוחנן's question. His answer is that the top of the wall counts as רשות היחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wall has the power to turn the area around it into a private domain. If it can do that for other space, it can certainly give its own top the same status. So landing an object on it makes the thrower חייב, even though it is less than four wide.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lesser case to a greater one ('all the more so')
a partition / wall that defines a domain

phrases.english: Ulla said: it is an a fortiori inference,
for others it makes a partition,
for itself, all the more so!?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wall's top counts as רשות היחיד, so the thrower is חייב.

steps.title: A report confirms the ruling of חייב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a report from רב and from רבי יוחנן himself that in this case the thrower is חייב, using the same קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב, and also רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If a wall in the public domain is ten טפחים high and less than four wide, and it surrounds a כרמלית and turns it into a private domain, then one who throws an object that lands on top of it is חייב. If it makes a partition for others, surely it does so for itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports עולא's answer. It quotes a teaching in the names of רב and רבי יוחנן that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the ruling of חייב, with the very same reasoning. It is notable that רבי יוחנן, who asked the question, is reported as ruling חייב. That shows his question was resolved this way.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated (a supporting report)

steps.whatToRemember: A wall ten טפחים high that creates a רשות היחיד counts as private domain itself, even if it is less than four wide. Throwing onto it makes one חייב.

phrases.english: It was also stated,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and likewise Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A wall in the public domain
ten high and not four wide
that surrounds a karmelit and made it a private domain,
and one threw and it landed on top of it — he is liable.
For others it makes a partition,
for itself, all the more so!?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports עולא's answer with a parallel statement.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's ruling that throwing onto the narrow wall makes one חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A report from רבי חייא בר אשי in the name of רב, and from רבי יצחק in the name of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Digging out earth that deepens a pit to ten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks: if a pit is nine טפחים deep and one lifts out a chunk of earth that makes it ten, is he חייב when the lifting and the partition happen at the same moment?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked: There is a pit nine טפחים deep. Someone lifts out a chunk of earth from it and so completes its depth to ten. What is the law? The lifting of the object and the making of the partition come at the same time. Is he חייב or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי יוחנן asks about a case where the act of lifting is the very act that turns the pit into a רשות היחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit becomes a private domain only once it is ten טפחים deep. Here, lifting the earth (the עקירה) is what makes it ten deep. So the question is whether it counts as lifting from a private domain when it was not yet private before the lifting began.

keyTerms.meaning: lifting the object (the start of carrying)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked:
a pit nine deep, and one lifted a segment from it
and completed it to ten — what is the law?
phrases.notes: He then throws the earth into the public domain.

phrases.english: The lifting of the object and the making of the partition
come together at the same time,
is he liable or not liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question from רבי יוחנן on a different issue.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the עקירה and the creation of the ten-טפחים partition happen at once, is one חייב?

steps.title: Putting earth into a pit and making it shallow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks a follow-up: even if the first case is פטור, what about a ten-deep pit where putting in earth makes it less than ten?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that he is not חייב because the partition was not ten טפחים from the start, then what about a pit ten טפחים deep? Someone puts a chunk of earth into it and makes it less deep. What is the law? The placing of the object and the removal of the partition come at the same time. Is he חייב or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן builds a second question on top of the first. He asks about the reverse case, where the partition exists at the start but disappears at the moment of placing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the partition was missing at the start. Here it is present at the start, while the object is flying in, and it vanishes only at the moment of הנחה. So even if the first case is פטור, this one could be different. The next steps try to resolve this question.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you conclude (a follow-up built on one answer)
placing down the object (the end of carrying)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate, unrelated question. It is a 'step two' that only applies if the first case is ruled פטור.

phrases.english: And if you say

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוֵי מְחִיצָה עֲשָׂרָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
phrases.english: since the partition was not ten from the beginning
he is not liable:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹר עֲשָׂרָה וְנָתַן לְתוֹכָהּ חוּלְיָא וּמִיעֲטָהּ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: a pit ten deep, and he put a segment into it and reduced it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The earth is thrown in from the public domain.

phrases.english: The placing of the object and the removal of the partition
come together at the same time,
is he liable or not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question that assumes the first case of Step 12 is פטור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the הנחה and the removal of the ten-טפחים partition happen at once, is one חייב?

steps.title: Proposed proof from the משנה about throwing at a wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests answering רבי יוחנן's question from his own statement. It quotes a משנה about throwing at a wall, the question 'it didn't rest there', and רבי יוחנן's answer that the case is a juicy fig cake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve it from his own words, as we learned in a משנה: if someone throws something four אמות and it hits a wall above ten טפחים, it is like throwing into the air. If it hits below ten, it is like throwing onto the ground, and someone who throws four אמות onto the ground is חייב. We asked about this: but the object did not rest there! And רבי יוחנן said: the משנה is talking about a juicy fig cake that sticks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins an attempt to answer רבי יוחנן's question by bringing a משנה and רבי יוחנן's own explanation of it. This step lays out the source; the next step will show how it answers the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting a wall below ten טפחים normally does not count as 'resting', because the object bounces off. So רבי יוחנן explained that the משנה means a sticky fig cake that stays on the wall. That gives a real הנחה, a proper placement of the object.

keyTerms.meaning: Like throwing into the air (no landing, so פטור)
But it didn't come to rest!
A juicy, sticky cake of pressed figs

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ten-טפחים lines. Above ten on a wall in רשות הרבים is an exempt area, so it counts as 'air'. Below ten counts as the ground of רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Resolve it for him from his own (words), as we learned:
One who throws four cubits at a wall,
above ten handbreadths — it is like throwing into the air.
phrases.notes: He is פטור.

phrases.english: Below ten — it is like throwing onto the ground,
and one who throws four cubits onto the ground is liable.
And we discussed it: but it did not come to rest!

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּדְבֵילָה שְׁמֵינָה שָׁנִינוּ.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: we learned it about a juicy fig cake.
phrases.notes: It sticks to the wall, so it does rest there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבי יוחנן's question from step 13 using his own earlier ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's question about placing an object at the same moment a partition is removed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about throwing at a wall, as explained by רבי יוחנן (fig cake)

steps.title: The fig cake shortens the distance, yet he is still liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the fig cake shrinks the four-אמות distance at the moment it lands. Since רבי יוחנן still holds the thrower חייב, a placement that happens at the same moment as a change in the measurement must count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is he liable? The fig cake reduces the distance from four אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the point of the proof. The fig cake's own thickness cuts down the distance it traveled, yet רבי יוחנן still says the thrower is חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fig cake becomes part of the wall, the wall now sticks out a little, so the throw is slightly less than four אמות. That reduction happens at the very moment of the הנחה. Since he is still חייב, a placement counts even when it happens together with a change to the boundary, and the same should apply to earth put into the pit.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַמַּאי? הָא קָא מְמַעֵט מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: And why (is he liable)? It reduces (the distance) from four cubits!
phrases.notes: So he must be liable even though landing and shrinking happen together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? הָא קָא מְמַעֵט מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual inference from the source quoted in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: Placement at the same moment a partition is removed still counts as liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן holds the thrower חייב with the fig cake even though it shortens the distance

steps.title: The fig cake is not nullified, but the earth is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The fig cake is not made part of the wall, so it does not really shorten the distance. Earth placed in a pit is made part of the pit and truly changes its depth.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he does not nullify it. Here, he nullifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the two cases are different, so the proof does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody treats a fig cake stuck to a wall as part of the wall; it will be taken off later. So the four אמות are never really reduced. Earth thrown into a pit becomes part of the pit floor (it is בטל to it), so it really changes the depth. רבי יוחנן's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifies, makes it part of something else

steps.whatToRemember: A placed item changes the boundary only if it becomes part of it (בטל). A sticky fig cake does not; earth in a pit does.

phrases.english: There, he does not nullify it.
phrases.notes: The fig cake stays a separate item.

phrases.english: Here, he nullifies it.
phrases.notes: The earth becomes part of the pit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא מְבַטֵּל לַהּ. הָכָא מְבַטֵּל לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 14-15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the fig cake and the earth in the pit
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fig cake is never nullified to the wall, so it does not truly change the boundary

steps.title: רבא asks about a board landing on stakes
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about someone who throws a board that lands on stakes ten טפחים tall but narrow. When the board lands, it creates a four-wide surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if someone threw a board and it landed on top of stakes, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question. A board lands on narrow stakes, and its landing creates a wide enough surface to be a רשות היחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stakes alone are too narrow to be a private domain. Once the board lands on top, there is a surface ten high and four wide. So the board's landing and the creation of the private domain happen at the same moment.

phrases.english: Rava asked:

phrases.aramaic: זָרַק דַּף וְנָח עַל גַּבֵּי יְתֵידוֹת, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If he threw a board and it landed on top of stakes, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The stakes are ten high but less than four wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: זָרַק דַּף וְנָח עַל גַּבֵּי יְתֵידוֹת, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question on the same theme of things happening at the same moment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the thrower חייב when the board's landing itself creates the private domain it lands in?

steps.title: This seems to be the same as רבי יוחנן's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's question. If it is about placement and making a partition at the same moment, רבי יוחנן already asked that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is he asking? Whether placing the object and making the partition happen together? That is רבי יוחנן's question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: his question seems to repeat what רבי יוחנן already asked. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will show what is new in רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's pit case, lifting the earth both moved the object and made the pit ten deep at once. רבא's board also lands and creates the domain at once. The challenge is that רבא would not need to ask a question that was already asked, so his question must be about something different.

phrases.english: What is his question?
(Whether) placing the object and making the partition
come together at the same time?
That is the same as Rabbi Yochanan's (question)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's question from step 17 by comparing it to רבי יוחנן's question in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's question about the board on stakes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the question is about placement and making a partition at the same moment, it repeats רבי יוחנן's question in step 12, so רבא would not need to ask it.

steps.title: רבא's real question: a board with an object riding on top
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רבא's question. He is asking about a board thrown with an object sitting on it: do they land at the same moment, or does the board land first?
steps.simpleTranslation: What רבא was really asking about is a case where someone threw a board with an object on top of it. What is the law? Since the board and the object arrive together, maybe it is like the object being placed and the partition being made at the same moment. Or maybe, since the object must lift up a little and then settle down, it is like the partition being made first and the object being placed afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge from Step 18. רבא was not repeating רבי יוחנן's question. He was asking about a different case: a board thrown with an object resting on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the board and the object truly land as one, this is exactly רבי יוחנן's unresolved case of הנחה and מחיצה happening at once. But the object is not attached to the board, so it may bounce up a tiny bit and land a split second later. In that case the מחיצה already exists before the object lands, and the thrower would clearly be חייב. רבא's question is which picture is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not asking whether simultaneous הנחה and מחיצה make one חייב. That is רבי יוחנן's question. רבא is asking whether this case counts as simultaneous in the first place.

phrases.english: When Rava was asking (it was about)

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּזָרַק דַּף וְחֵפֶץ עַל גַּבָּיו, מַאי?
phrases.english: a case where one threw a board with an object on top of it. What is the law?
Since they come together
it is like placing the object and making the partition (at the same moment)
phrases.notes: This is the same as רבי יוחנן's unresolved question.

phrases.english: Or perhaps:
since it is impossible
for it not to lift up a little and then come to rest
it is like making the partition first and then placing the object.
phrases.notes: Partition first, then placement means the thrower is clearly חייב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18's challenge by redefining what רבא's question was about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא of the question)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's question was simply about simultaneous placement and partition, which רבי יוחנן already asked.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא asks whether a board carrying a loose object counts as simultaneous at all, or whether the partition comes first.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבא's question without an answer: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has no answer to רבא's question about the board and the object, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means neither side is proven. We do not know whether the object lands together with the board or just after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's question (simultaneous הנחה and מחיצה) and רבא's question (does a board carrying a loose object count as simultaneous) both remain unresolved.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes Step 19's question with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question about the board and the object is left unresolved.

steps.title: רבא: water poured onto water counts as placed
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it is obvious that water landing on water counts as placed. He then begins to discuss a nut floating on water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is obvious to me that water on top of water counts as its placement. A nut on top of water...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic: when does something landing on water count as placed? He first states the obvious case, and then he begins to set up the next case, a nut on water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water poured onto water blends in and rests there, so it counts as a full הנחה. If someone did this from one רשות to another, he is חייב. A nut floating on water is less clear, because it drifts and does not truly rest. The discussion of the nut continues in the next part of the text.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is obvious to me
water on top of water —
that is its placement.
A nut on top of water —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related line of rulings by רבא about what counts as placement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water poured onto water counts as placed. The status of a nut on water is about to be discussed.
